post.description: Create a new blocklist owned by your organization. The name must be unique within your organization. The list will only be visible to your organization and organizations you shared the blocklist with. This operation is submitted to quotas

get.description: Get multiple blocklists. Only blocklists owned by your organization, shared with your organization or public blocklists are returned. Filters and pagination are available as query parameters.

parameters.name: include_filter

schema.description: Include blocklists with the specified filters
schema.title: Include Filter

parameters.description: Include blocklists with the specified filters

get.description: Get the details of a blocklist by ID. The content of the blocklist is not returned.

patch.description: Update a blocklist's details by ID. It is not possible to update the blocklist content using this operation.

delete.description: Delete a blocklist by ID. If the blocklist is shared with other organizations or it has subscriptions, the operation will fail. If you want to force delete the blocklist, you can use the force query parameter, so the blocklists will be unshared / unsubscribed.

parameters.name: force

schema.description: Force delete the blocklist if it is shared or subscribed
schema.title: Force

parameters.description: Force delete the blocklist if it is shared or subscribed

post.description: Upload a blocklist. The file must be in txt format with one IP per line. This operation will overwrite the existing blocklist content.

400.description: Invalid IP in blocklist file content

post.description: Add IPs to a blocklist. If an IP is already in the blocklist, its expiration will be updated with the new expiration.

412.description: Payload too large for one operation, limit is 20000 IPs per request
Payload too large for one operation, limit is 20000 IPs per request

get.description: Download blocklist content as a list of ips as plain text separated by new lines. The response will include the ETag header for cache control. If_Modified_Since and If_None_Match cache control headers are supported for conditional requests.

post.description: Subscribe to a blocklist with a remediation type. If the entity type is the full organization or a Tag, all the engines belonging to the organization or the Tag will be subscribed and new engines that will join the organization or the Tag will also be automatically subscribed. If the subscription has been done on an organization or Tag you cannot unsubscribe individual engines. In case of errors for some subscribers, the operation will still succeed for the entities that were successfully subscribed and you'll have the list of errors in the operation's result. This operation is submitted to quotas.

get.description: Get blocklist subscribers within your organization.

delete.description: Unsubscribe from a blocklist. You cannot unsubscribe individual engines if the subscription has been done on an organization or Tag.

post.description: Share a blocklist with other organizations given their IDs. The blocklist must be owned by your organization. You can give read-only access or read-write access to the blocklist. Sharing a blocklist will not automatically subscribe the shared organizations to the blocklist.

delete.description: Unshare a blocklist with other organizations. If the blocklist is subscribed by the organization, the operation will fail.Use force query parameter to unshare a blocklist even if subscriptions exists.

post.description: Create an integration to a firewall or remediation component, owned by your organization. The name should be unique within the organization. This operation is submitted to quotas.

get.description: Get integrations owned by your organization

parameters.name: tag

schema.description: List of tags associated with the integrations (any of)
schema.title: Tag

parameters.description: List of tags associated with the integrations (any of)

get.description: Get an integration by ID

parameters.name: force

schema.description: Force delete the integration even if it has active subscriptions (it will unsubscribe from all lists)
schema.title: Force

head.description: Check if the integration has content

204.description: Integration has no subscribed blocklists or no content available

get.description: Get the ips associated to the integration in plain text format. The content can be paginated to accomodate limits in firewalls.

parameters.name: page_size

schema.description: Maximum number of items to return, 0 means no limit (default), should be greater than 10000
schema.title: Page Size

parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return, 0 means no limit (default), should be greater than 10000

204.description: Integration has no subscribed blocklists or no content available

get.description: Get the ips associated to the integration in a format compatible with a remediation component. As for the remediation components, you can fetch the full content with startup=true or only the changes since the last pull

parameters.name: startup

schema.description: Set to true if it's the first run to fetch all the content, otherwise only changes since the last pull.
schema.title: Startup

get.description:
Get a (minimized) index file for 'cscli hub update'. May or may not include unused fields
(content, long descriptions, labels...) or redundant ones (author, name).
get.summary: Get a minimized index file (crowdsec only)

head.description:
This endpoint returns cache-related headers for the index file without the full content.
It is useful for validating cache, checking resource freshness, and managing client-side
cache expiration policies. No body content is returned.
head.summary: Check cache control headers for the index file

get.description: Get an item's content from its path. This is usually a YAML file.

This endpoint returns cache-related headers for an item's content. It is useful for validating
cache, checking resource freshness, and managing client-side cache expiration policies. No body
content is returned.

type: leaky
#debug: true
name: crowdsecurity/vsftpd-bf
description: "Detect FTP bruteforce (vsftpd)"
filter: evt.Meta.log_type == 'ftp_failed_auth'
leakspeed: "10s"
capacity: 5
groupby: evt.Meta.source_ip
blackhole: 5m
labels:
  confidence: 3
  spoofable: 0
  classification:
    - attack.T1110
  behavior: "ftp:bruteforce"
  label: "VSFTPD Bruteforce"
  remediation: true
  service: vsftpd

filter: evt.Meta.log_type == 'ftp_failed_auth'
leakspeed: "10s"
capacity: 5
groupby: evt.Meta.source_ip
blackhole: 5m
labels:
  confidence: 3
  spoofable: 0
  classification:
    - attack.T1110
  behavior: "ftp:bruteforce"
  label: "VSFTPD Bruteforce"
  remediation: true
  service: vsftpd

IndicatorHttpPath.title: IndicatorHttpPath
IndicatorHttpPath.description:
One HTTP-path indicator (a single row from http_path_context).

``value`` is the reconstructed HTTP request line: ``"<METHOD> <PATH>"``
(e.g. ``"POST /wp-login.php"``). Future indicator types use the same
``value`` field with different semantics — clients dispatch on
``indicator_type``.

The internal scoring columns ``watcher_count`` and ``cve_count`` drive
SQL filtering/ranking but are never exposed. ``pokemon_count`` is
surfaced as ``nb_ips`` so the API speaks in user-facing terms.

IndicatorType.title: IndicatorType
IndicatorType.description:
Kind of IOC carried in an indicator entry. Add new variants here
as we extend coverage (user_agent, ja3h, …).

IndicatorsSortBy.title: IndicatorsSortBy
IndicatorsSortBy.description:
How the caller wants the indicators ordered.

``popular`` returns the cache's ``popular`` slice; ``most_recent`` returns
the ``recent`` slice. Both come pre-ranked from the Athena query so the
API doesn't re-sort.
